fix: pair Turnstile site key with configured secret and harden inquiry endpoint

Two independent faults kept the inquiry form broken:

1. Wrong Turnstile widget. src/config.ts shipped a site key
   (0x4AAAAAAEow16pcFLjiXJag) that did not belong to the widget whose
   secret key is configured in Cloudflare Pages. The browser therefore
   solved one widget while the server verified another, so every real
   submission ended in "Spam verification failed."

2. No upstream timeout. A hanging fetch to Resend aborted the whole
   Pages Function, and Cloudflare replaced the JSON error with its own
   HTML 502 page (text/html + retry-after: 60). The browser then threw
   "Unexpected token '<'" while parsing it.

Changes:
- src/config.ts: point siteKey at the widget actually linked to the
  configured secret (0x4AAAAAAEow1zs0l4GoQsPEcCn29853OAo)
- functions/api/inquiry.ts:
  * fail with 503 JSON when RESEND_API_KEY / INQUIRY_TO_EMAIL are missing
    instead of logging and returning ok:true, which silently dropped leads
  * abort the Resend request after 8s and report a JSON 502, so the
    runtime never gets killed mid-request
  * log the upstream status and body on rejection
- src/components/InquiryForm.astro: read the response as text and parse
  it, so a non-JSON gateway error can no longer surface as
  "Unexpected token '<'"
- tools/test-inquiry.mjs: smoke test for the endpoint, runnable against
  local wrangler or production via BASE=...
- docs/deployment-cloudflare.md: updated site key, note that the site key
  and secret key must come from the same widget

fix: restore correct Turnstile site key (was confused with the secret key)

The previous commit swapped the widget's two keys. On the Turnstile
widget page:

  Site key   = 0x4AAAAAAEow16pcFLjiXJag   (browser, public)  <- original value
  Secret key = 0x4AAAAAAEow1zs0l4GoQsPEcCn29853OAo (server-side)

Both start with "0x" and look nearly identical, so the secret was
mistaken for the site key and shipped in src/config.ts. A browser
widget initialized with the secret generates tokens the siteverify
endpoint always rejects.

This restores the original (correct) site key and documents the
site-key-vs-secret-key pitfall in the deployment guide. The server
side expects TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY to hold the widget's secret key.

fix: cover response body reads inside the upstream abort windows

The previous hardening aborted the Resend fetch after 8s, but the timer
was cleared as soon as response HEADERS arrived - the body read
(res.text()) ran unguarded afterwards, and verifyTurnstile had no
timeout at all. An upstream that sends headers and then stalls on the
body therefore hung the Worker past the runtime limits, and Cloudflare
replaced the JSON error with its own HTML 502 page. The browser side
then reported "[inquiry] Non-JSON response 502", i.e. "Submission
failed" - observed live today.

Changes:
- Resend call: fetch AND res.text() now run inside one try guarded by
  the 8s AbortController; clearTimeout moved to a finally block
- verifyTurnstile: same pattern with a 5s abort around siteverify,
  covering its res.json() body read too
- timing + abort markers added to the console diagnostics so a
  wrangler tail shows exactly where and how fast an upstream failed

fix: set preferred canonical host to www.zzpine.com

The bare domain was used everywhere, so canonical, hreflang, og:url and the
sitemap all advertised zzpine.com while the site will be served with the bare
domain 301-redirecting to www. Better to settle this before launch than to
re-point the canonical afterwards.

Updated: astro.config.mjs site, config.ts SITE.url, robots.txt Sitemap line,
plus the deployment guide, which now records www as the decided host.

Verified in the build output: canonical, hreflang alternates, og:url, sitemap
entries and robots.txt all use https://www.zzpine.com; zero bare-domain
references remain. Build: 770 pages.
docs: add Cloudflare Pages deployment guide (domain stays on Aliyun)

fix: resolve committed merge conflict markers and restore build

The merge commit fd201c3 landed with unresolved conflict markers inside
seven source files, which broke 'astro build' outright. Both sides of
every conflict came from two architectures: HEAD carries the thin English
wrappers plus the 11-language i18n system, while cyrustse carried the older
single-language page bodies whose content was already absorbed into
src/templates/. Took the HEAD side everywhere and dropped the dead bodies.

Follow-on fixes the merge exposed:
- templates/PowerPage.astro still referenced the removed singular
  POWER_CATEGORY_PARENT; it now takes parentCategory through props, matching
  PowerListing.astro and the route wrappers.
- Both [power].astro wrappers and the [lang] dynamic route now pass
  parentCategory down.
- BaseLayout.astro lost the CONTACT import in the merge, but the
  Organization contactPoint block reads CONTACT.phone/.email, so the import
  is restored.

Build: 770 pages, no broken internal links, sitemap complete.
